pr_title: drivers: clock_control: stm32f7 force flash latency with overdrive
pr_body:
The Flash latency depends on the sysclock but also in case of the stm32F7 on the regulator overdrive mode. The overdrive must be set before the first LL_SetFlashLatency.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/50853

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments: i just tested it on our board and it fixes the problem

moving the change (overdrive mode) out of the control of the Flash Latency 
`#if defined(FLASH_ACR_LATENCY)`

> 
> The reference manual (4.1.4 Voltage Regulator) recommend to switch to overdrive mode only when clocked from HSI or HSE. Calling `stm32_clock_switch_to_hsi()` before configuring OVD Mode solved the problem (like for PLL configuration).

If we follow this recommendation, we should see in the stm32_clock_control_init()

1. set_up_fixed_clock_sources()
2. set fixed clock as sysclock source
3. enable overdrive
4. setFlash Latency
5. set_up_plls()
6. set sysclock source

review_comments: LGTM, but in order to ease future maintenance, I would have move this block (STM32_PLL_ENABLED && CONFIG_SOC_SERIES_STM32F7X) before FLASH_ACR_LATENCY block (to avoid imbrication of both compilation switches)

Yes, 
activation of the overdrive mode depends on the sys clock freq (whatever the latency but must be done before the latency setting)
